text:
sanjay: heads up — someone dropped a new model in the intake queue: repo https://git.example.com/models/garnet-6b. License file says `Garnet-Community-NC-1.0`. unsure what that means for hosting.

liz-legal: thanks for the ping. 'NC' usually = non-commercial. need to see full license text and any third-party data attributions. can you paste the LICENSE and model card?

maria-ml: pasted the model card in the intake form, but here's the LICENSE header: `Garnet-Community-NC-1.0 — This license permits research and internal use; commercial use prohibited without separate agreement.`

onboarding-bot: license-scan: status=warning; id=GARNET-NC-1.0; matched_terms=["non-commercial", "no redistribution for profit"]; recommend=legal-review.

kevin-ml: from infra perspective: if it's NC, that blocks hosted API and dedicated public pools. Private deployments (customer-managed infra) might be ok if contract ensures no commercial use. but we need legal confirmation.

jordan-sec: also check export control tags — model weights originate from dataset with EU components, possible ECCN? I can run export scan but will need provenance files.

liz-legal: agree with kevin. preliminary read: we cannot offer Garnet-6B via our hosted API or include in Marketplace. Private deployments may be possible under contract that prohibits customers from commercializing outputs. need to check compatibility with our terms and whether the third-party dataset requires attribution or has further restrictions.

sanjay: ok. high-level asks: 1) can eng-ml run quantization/eval experiments internally for perf/quality? 2) can we include Garnet-6B in internal benchmark comparisons? 3) what blockers for adding to model catalog as 'internal-only'?

maria-ml: 1) yes for internal experiments (research/non-prod) — that's permitted under NC as long as we don't monetize. 2) internal benching is fine, but results shared externally need license-safe wording. 3) catalog: we can add a private/internal tag but the onboarding UI needs a 'usage_restriction' flag. currently tracked as `restricted_license=non-commercial` in intake form.

liz-legal: confirm: internal benchmarking and evals are OK. external publication of results is allowed only if we redact any parts covered by third-party obligations and avoid implying commercial use. if we want to allow partner testing, we'd need bespoke agreements.

jordan-sec: for export control: ran quick provenance check, dataset manifest missing some upstream attributions. I flagged a ticket (SEC-4823) to request upstream manifests from the repo owner. until that's resolved we should not distribute weights outside org.

kevin-ml: action items for infra/devex: add an intake enforcement rule to block hosted deploys for models with `restricted_license=non-commercial`. toggles: allow-internal-quantize=true, allow-private-deployments=manual-approval.

sanjay: i'll file a short RFC to add the flag to the onboarding flow and add a step to require legal signoff for NC/ND licenses. will also schedule a short sync with liz and jordan.

liz-legal: for the sync, can we include a sample contract clause for private deployments? i can draft a template limiting commercial exploitation + audit rights.

maria-ml: quick note on quantization: we tried 4-bit QAT on a forked checkpoint yesterday — quality drop ~1.2 BLEU-equivalent on internal tasks. if we have legal OK, we should run the more thorough ruler/eval harness to verify regressions before any catalog entry.

onboarding-bot: ticket created: ML-INTAKE-9123 (license: GARNET-NC-1.0) assigned to liz-legal.

sanjay: thanks everyone. next steps: liz to confirm hosting restrictions in PR, jordan to complete export manifest check, kevin to add intake guardrail, maria to run full eval after legal signoff. ping me in-thread when done. :thumbsup:
